# Iterator instructions

The `.iterator` stack holds first-class loops: a source (a range, a collection or a block), a cursor, and optionally a body to run each pass. Iterators are how the language counts, walks collections and collects results.

## The stack's own instructions

Every stack has the same family for copying, deleting, reordering and measuring its items; see <doc:StackInstructions>. On `.iterator` they are `iteratorDeepDup`, `iteratorDeleteAtDepth`, `iteratorDup`, `iteratorDupItems`, `iteratorDupTimes`, `iteratorFlush`, `iteratorPop`, `iteratorPopItems`, `iteratorRot`, `iteratorShove`, `iteratorStackDepth`, `iteratorStackIsEmpty`, `iteratorSwap`, `iteratorYank`, `iteratorYankDup`.
